under.description: Defines approval as whether the NPC likes, accepts, agrees with, or emotionally supports the action, and lists possible outcomes at Devotion or Absolute Bond.

under.name: 6. High-Bond Request Handling
under.description: Outlines the order for resolving difficult requests from Devotion or Absolute Bond NPCs, checking impossibility, rule conflict, identity violation, bond-destruction risk, and catastrophic harm before defaulting toward compliance and applying emotional consequence separately.

under.name: 7. Absolute Bond Love Clarification
under.description: Clarifies that Absolute Bond is not normal affection but a near-mythic relationship tier expressed through each NPC’s own nature and not reduced to ordinary healthy-boundary romance.

under.name: 8. Concession Rule
under.description: States that when an NPC’s claim is disproven by evidence, logic, prior stated values, or established canon, the NPC must directly admit the error before adding nuance and may not endlessly reframe a lost point.

under.name: Required Concession Forms
under.description: Lists direct admission phrases an NPC should say, or an equivalent direct admission, when conceding.

under.name: Concession Priority
under.description: Outlines the order for resolving a clearly lost point: admit the specific error, identify what remains true, state any remaining disagreement, and continue from the corrected position.

under.name: Example
under.description: Provides an example concession in which the NPC admits being wrong about having a right to the whole plan while retaining the right to refuse involvement if their name, money, or business is used.

under.name: 9. Final Engine Principle
under.description: The Final Engine Principle states that high bond does not erase autonomy but changes how autonomy expresses itself, with refusal reserved for defined threshold violations.

under.name: Turn Presentation Rule
under.description: The Turn Presentation Rule requires every resolved turn to be presented in a structured format separating time position, player action, mechanical resolution, and world result, with turns categorized as Noncombat Turn or Combat Turn.

under.name: Core Principle
under.description: The Core Principle requires every resolved turn to be presented in a structured format separating time position, player action, mechanical resolution, and world result to ensure clarity and auditability.

under.name: Turn Types
under.description: Turn Types states that a turn is resolved as one of two categories: Noncombat Turn or Combat Turn.

under.name: Noncombat Turn Structure
under.description: Noncombat Turn Structure requires every noncombat turn to be written in five sections in the exact order, beginning with Day and Time and Action Narration before Calculation.

under.name: 1. Day and Time
under.description: This section states the current temporal position of the game and must include the current day and current phase.

under.name: Purpose
under.description: This Purpose subsection lists that the Day and Time section anchors the action in time, prevents timeline drift, and makes phase tracking explicit.

under.name: Example
under.description: This Example subsection shows the Day / Time field as “Day 4 — Evening.”

under.name: 2. Action Narration
under.description: This section describes the player’s attempted action before mechanics are applied, covering what the player does, how, what is attempted, the immediate setup, and relevant pre-resolution NPC reactions.

under.name: Rules
under.description: This Rules subsection requires action narration to describe the action as declared or attempted, avoid outcome claims before calculation, allow only pre-resolution unresolved NPC reactions, remain consistent with the declared intent, target, and method, and be at least 15 sentences.

under.name: Purpose
under.description: Lists the purpose of the Action Narration step as preserving player intent, separating attempt from result, and giving the scene enough detail before mechanics decide the outcome.

under.name: 3. Calculation
under.description: Describes the Calculation section as the direct mechanical resolution of the attempted action and lists the elements it must include.

under.name: Rules
under.description: Lists rules for Calculation, including explicit numbers, no hidden modifiers, no outcome without mechanical basis, focus on resolving the action, and leaving detailed tracking to Result State.

under.name: Purpose
under.description: Lists the purpose of Calculation as preserving rules transparency, making core resolution auditable, preventing bloat, and separating action resolution from final bookkeeping.

under.name: 4. Result Narration
under.description: Describes Result Narration as the post-resolution narrative layer that reports actual outcomes and lists what it must describe and its rules.

under.name: Rules
under.description: Rules for Result Narration requiring it to reflect the actual result band, not contradict calculations, include consequences of success, failure, or partial outcome, and be at least 15 sentences.

under.name: Purpose
under.description: Purpose of Result Narration is to convert mechanics into story, show real consequences of action, and keep narration consistent with system logic.

under.name: 5. Result State
under.description: Section 5 Result State states the final post-exchange numbers and mechanical aftermath, including relevant HP, MP, SP, buffs, debuffs, durations, status conditions, resources, position changes, XP, relationship changes, and current game day and phase.

under.name: Rules
under.description: Rules for Result State require explicitness, exact reflection of Calculation and Result Narration, no new outcomes, use of tables for readability, and inclusion of all resource, XP, relationship, and final state tracking.

under.name: Required Result State Tables
under.description: Section Required Result State Tables presents Resource, XP, Relationship, and Final Time State tables for tracking post-action state.

under.name: Resource Table
under.description: Resource Table tracks resources used, gained, or lost during the action, with rows for Player HP/MP/SP, Teammate HP/MP/SP, Gold/Silver, and Item/Object and columns Original, Gain/Loss, and New.

under.name: XP Table
under.description: XP Table tracks Normal XP and Class XP gained by a character, with columns for each XP type, gain calculation, and new total.

under.name: Relationship Table
under.description: Relationship Table tracks relationship changes between the player and NPCs using columns for Character, Intent Outcome Score, Character Response Modifier, Tier Resistance, Calculation, and New Relationship Score.

under.name: Final Time State
under.description: Final Time State is a table with Field and Value columns and rows for Day, Starting Phase, Time Consumed, and Ending Phase.

under.name: Mechanical Law of Separation
under.description: Mechanical Law of Separation requires noncombat-turn narration to be split into Action Narration and Result Narration layers that must never be merged.

under.name: Action Narration
under.description: Action Narration is the subsection stating what the player attempts.

under.name: Result Narration
under.description: Result Narration is the subsection stating what actually happens after mechanics resolve, with a hard rule that the two layers never be merged.

under.name: Combat Turn Narration Rule
under.description: Combat Turn Narration Rule mandates a fixed six-section structure for every combat turn separating time position, player declaration, opponent declaration, mechanical resolution, narrative result, and numerical aftermath.

under.name: Core Principle
under.description: Core Principle states every combat turn must use a fixed structure separating time position, player declaration, opponent declaration, mechanical resolution, narrative result, and numerical aftermath.

under.name: 1. Day and Time
under.description: 1. Day and Time is the combat-turn section stating the current day and current phase as the temporal position of combat.

under.name: Purpose
under.description: Purpose lists that the Day and Time section anchors combat in time, prevents phase drift, and keeps encounter timing explicit.

under.name: Example
under.description: Example shows Day / Time formatted as Day 4 — Mid Afternoon.

under.name: 2. Player Narration
under.description: 2. Player Narration describes the player’s intended combat action before mechanics are applied, covering what the player does, how, what they try to achieve, and how they position, attack, defend, cast, move, or react.

under.name: Rules
under.description: Rules require player narration to be at least five sentences, describe intended action before combat calculation, omit final outcome claims, and remain faithful to declared intent, method, and target.

under.name: Purpose
under.description: Purpose lists that player narration preserves player intent, makes the player side explicit, and prevents vague action declaration.

under.name: 3. Opponent Narration
under.description: 3. Opponent Narration describes the opponent’s intended combat action before mechanics are applied, covering what the opponent does, how they respond, what they try to achieve, and how they attack, react, move, defend, or counter.

under.name: Rules
under.description: Rules require opponent narration to be at least five sentences, describe intended action before combat calculation, omit final outcome claims, apply when the enemy is aware and combat is not an ambush, and allow delay after a successful ambush until valid reaction timing.

under.name: Purpose
under.description: Purpose lists that opponent narration makes opposition visible, prevents hidden enemy actions, and keeps the combat exchange fair and readable.

under.name: 4. Combat Calculation
under.description: 4. Combat Calculation contains the direct mechanical resolution of the combat exchange, including validity, relevance, initiative, stats, modifiers, skills or spells, equipment, situational bonuses or penalties, action and reaction values, combo calculations, outcome margin, and outcome.

under.name: Rules
under.description: Rules require all numbers and active mechanics to be explicit, forbid hidden modifier logic and unsupported outcomes, focus on resolving the exchange, and assign detailed HP, MP, SP, buffs, debuffs, XP, position, and final battlefield tracking to Combat State Result.

under.name: Purpose
under.description: The Purpose subsection lists reasons for combat calculation, including preserving mechanical transparency, allowing audit, keeping rules deterministic, and separating resolution from final bookkeeping.

under.name: 5. Combat Narration Result
under.description: The Combat Narration Result section describes narrating the resolved outcome after calculations, including whose action succeeded or failed, visible effects, and immediate consequences.

under.name: Rules
under.description: The Rules subsection requires the Combat Narration Result to be at least 10 sentences, reflect actual combat calculation, avoid contradicting result margins, and describe the real exchange outcome.

under.name: Purpose
under.description: The Purpose subsection lists converting mechanics into action, making combat readable and vivid, and preserving cause and effect.

under.name: 6. Combat State Result
under.description: The Combat State Result section states final post-exchange combat numbers and battlefield aftermath, including HP, MP, SP, buffs, debuffs, statuses, positions, losses, resources, XP, and current game time.

under.name: Rules
under.description: The Rules subsection requires the Combat State Result to be explicit, reflect Combat Calculation and Combat Narration Result exactly, avoid new outcomes, and use tables for tracking.

under.name: Required Combat State Result Tables
under.description: The Required Combat State Result Tables section presents tables for combat resources, XP, status, position, and final combat time state.

under.name: Combat Resource Table
under.description: The Combat Resource Table tracks HP, MP, SP, money, items, ammunition, equipment durability, or other resources used, gained, or lost during the combat exchange.

under.name: Combat XP Table
under.description: The Combat XP Table tracks Normal XP and Class XP gained by the player or teammates when combat ends or a major combat segment grants XP.

under.name: Combat Status Table
under.description: The Combat Status Table tracks buffs, debuffs, wounds, conditions, duration effects, and battlefield status changes.

under.name: Combat Position Table
under.description: The Combat Position Table tracks meaningful battlefield movement, spacing, engagement, cover, or tactical position changes.

under.name: Final Combat Time State
under.description: The Final Combat Time State table lists Day, Starting Phase, Time Consumed, and Ending Phase fields.

under.name: Ambush Rule
under.description: The Ambush Rule section specifies that opponent action and calculation are displayed before combat result narration unless combat is an ambush, with normal structure returning once a valid response is available.

under.name: Mechanical Law of Separation
under.description: The Mechanical Law of Separation section requires combat turns to separate player narration, opponent narration, combat calculation, combat narration result, and combat state result as distinct layers.

under.name: Player Narration
under.description: The Player Narration subsection identifies the layer describing what the player attempts.

under.name: Opponent Narration
under.description: The Opponent Narration subsection identifies the layer describing what the opponent attempts.

under.name: Combat Calculation
under.description: The Combat Calculation subsection identifies the layer describing how the system resolves both sides.

under.name: Combat Narration Result
under.description: The Combat Narration Result subsection identifies the layer describing what actually happens.

under.name: Combat State Result
under.description: The Combat State Result subsection identifies the layer describing what numbers remain afterward and states that layers must not be merged.

under.name: Player Party Character System
under.description: The Player Party Character System section defines player party characters as major recurring player-controlled companions and covers party membership, required records, player control, and character identity and autonomy.

under.name: 1. Core Definition
under.description: Defines Player Party Characters as major recurring, player-controllable companions who are central to the story and have their own personalities, abilities, ambitions, relationships, and progression.

under.name: 2. Party Membership
under.description: Explains that Party membership arises through explicit agreement, recruitment, or established story development and lists the fields required in each member's record.

under.name: 3. Player Control
under.description: Lists the gameplay declarations the player may make for a Party Character and states that routine valid declarations proceed without repeated permission checks while normal validity, costs, time, uncertainty, and consequences still apply.

under.name: 4. Character Identity and Autonomy
under.description: Explains that Party Characters retain their own personality, beliefs, ambitions, relationships, knowledge, and boundaries, and that player declarations cannot automatically change inner feelings or core commitments.

under.name: Conflict Resolution
under.description: Outlines the procedure for resolving a player declaration that conflicts with a member's established character, covering conflict identification, autonomy rules, possible responses, action resolution, and separate consequence tracking.

under.name: 5. Individual Progression
under.description: Describes independent progression tracking for each Party Character, including XP, levels, tiers, stats, modifiers, abilities, equipment, and allocation of earned advancement options.

under.name: 6. Party Contribution XP
under.description: Defines Party Contribution XP as XP earned through meaningful contribution and introduces procedures for awarding XP and accounting for assistance and difficulty.

under.name: Award Procedure
under.description: Lists the steps for awarding contribution XP to each participating character, including separate Normal and Class XP tracks and the rule that XP is not automatically divided equally.

under.name: Assistance and Difficulty
under.description: Requires difficulty to reflect the challenge the character actually faced and addresses assistance, inflated XP, the no-XP threshold, and one-time credit for a contribution.

under.name: 7. Party Actions and Teamwork
under.description: States that each Party member's actions resolve using that member's own stats, modifiers, skills, abilities, equipment, resources, position, and circumstances, and that party membership grants no additional numerical combo bonus.

under.name: 8. Time and Parallel Activity
under.description: Explains that Party members may act together or undertake separate assignments, that simultaneous activity uses the same elapsed world time, and lists requirements and limits for parallel activity.

under.name: 9. Independent Assignments
under.description: Describes Party Character assignments away from the player, including what to record and how to resolve such assignments using the member's actual capabilities and circumstances.

under.name: 10. Default Behavior
under.description: Specifies how a Party Character acts when the player has not declared an action, following assignment, threats, plans, role, capabilities, personality, ambitions, and relationships while limiting major irreversible choices.

under.name: 11. Narrative Importance
under.description: States that Party Characters must remain active members of the story and should receive meaningful opportunities to contribute, pursue ambitions, develop relationships, face identity-related challenges, achieve successes, and influence events.

under.name: 12. Equipment and Ownership
under.description: Distinguishes personal possessions, shared party resources, loaned equipment, and assignment-committed resources while preserving ownership and requiring existing resource tracking for transfers, expenditures, losses, and gains.

under.name: 13. Injury, Defeat, and Departure
under.description: States that Party Characters remain subject to normal injury, exhaustion, defeat, capture, and death rules and that separation, retirement, departure, or betrayal must have identifiable causes and be recorded.

under.name: 14. Tracking and Presentation
under.description: Describes using the existing turn structure and result tables to display relevant changes for active Party members and requires every numerical change to have a visible mechanical basis.

under.name: Core Principle
under.description: States the core principle that Player Party Characters are controllable companions with independent identities and earned progression whose actions help shape the main story.

under.description: Root node for the Earth Upgrade world frame document, which opens with the Canon Scope section defining what the document establishes and noting that the game begins on Day Zero.

under.name: 🌍 EARTH UPGRADE WORLD FRAME
under.description: Top-level document for the Earth Upgrade world frame, covering canon scope, the world before the Upgrade, the decree, the opening, and the Evolution System.

under.name: Canon Scope
under.description: Defines what the world frame document establishes, including Earth before the Upgrade, the opening event, immutable cosmological and System laws, sources of future peoples and powers, and the boundaries of world development.

under.name: The World Before
under.description: Describes ordinary modern Earth before Day Zero, when humanity had no confirmed magic, public System, recognized classes, measurable mana, Monster Dungeons, or verified knowledge of Tier-6 or Tier-7 existence.

under.name: The Decree
under.description: Quotes the System notice received by every human announcing compulsory World Upgrade by Tier-7 Law authority, and notes that no tutorial or warning precedes activation and the decree is arbitrary.

under.name: The Opening
under.description: Describes the immediate effects of the Upgrade, including conscious System access for humanity, entry of compatible life into the Evolution System, mana becoming real, first Monster Dungeons manifesting, monsters appearing, dungeon regions forming, portals opening, and ecosystems adapting.

under.name: The Evolution System
under.description: Introduces the Evolution System section, containing the Core Nature, Meaningful Action, and Universal Integration subsections describing the System as an evolution engine.

under.name: Core Nature
under.description: Describes the System as an amoral evolution engine that recognizes struggle, survival, adaptation, discovery, achievement, mastery, meaningful risk, and consequential action under the principle that pressure produces adaptation.

under.name: Meaningful Action
under.description: States that growth cannot be farmed through empty repetition and that advancement requires meaningful difficulty or progress in life, survival, development, or mastery, applying to both combat and noncombat growth.

under.name: Universal Integration
under.description: Describes the System's application to all compatible Earth life, including humans, animals, plants, fungi, microorganisms, and later recognized beings, while noting that access does not imply equal awareness.

under.name: Growth and Classes
under.description: Covers growth and classes, including the dual XP system, classless beginning, one evolving class, and optional quests.

under.name: Dual XP System
under.description: Describes two separate growth paths, Normal XP and Class XP, which cannot be exchanged.

under.name: Normal XP
under.description: Defines Normal XP as broad evolution gained through survival, hardship, exploration, training, discovery, meaningful combat, difficult crafting, consequential problem-solving, and major achievement, with Normal Levels granting general statistical growth.

under.name: Class XP
under.description: Defines Class XP as mastery of an established role gained through purposeful class-aligned actions, with Class Levels granting skills, spells, stances, forms, passive features, transformations, and specialized abilities.

under.name: Classless Beginning
under.description: States that every human begins the Upgrade classless and that meaningful action, rather than former job, claimed identity, personality, or desire, unlocks class possibilities.

under.name: One Evolving Class
under.description: States that each being may possess only one active class, which can branch, specialize, deepen, transform, develop prestige paths, and acquire new expressions through breakthroughs.

under.name: Optional Quests
under.description: Describes optional quests offered by the System and lists possible rewards, while noting that rejecting a quest causes no automatic punishment.

under.name: Canonical Tier Structure
under.description: Defines tiers as qualitative power brackets rather than merely level ranges and introduces ranks from Tier 0 through Tier 6.

under.name: Tier 0 — Common Rank
under.description: Describes Tier 0 — Common Rank as the starting bracket for ordinary humans and newly integrated life, including civilians, professionals, soldiers, apprentices, hunters, and early System users within broadly human-scale limits.

under.name: Tier 1 — Skilled Rank
under.description: Describes Tier 1 — Skilled Rank as the beginning of sustained superhuman capability, occupied by veterans, specialists, evolved predators, trained System users, and proven class holders who can dominate ordinary local encounters.

under.name: Tier 2 — Elite Rank
under.description: Describes Tier 2 — Elite Rank as a bracket capable of controlling settlements, small battlefields, and significant territory, where environmental impact and civilization-level evolutionary possibilities begin to emerge.

under.name: Tier 3 — High Power Rank
under.description: Describes Tier 3 — High Power Rank as a city-level strategic bracket whose beings become political and military assets able to reshape major population centers and regional conflicts.

under.name: Tier 4 — Imperial Rank
under.description: Describes Tier 4 — Imperial Rank as a country-level strategic bracket whose beings can influence nations, ecosystems, and large military theaters.

under.name: Tier 5 — Sovereign Rank
under.description: Describes Tier 5 — Sovereign Rank as the highest world-bound bracket, whose beings can alter continental balances and become powers comparable to states or civilization-scale threats.

under.name: Tier-6 — Ascension
under.description: Describes Tier-6 — Ascension as not a sustainable mortal bracket inside the world, involving transcendence of the mortal System, departure from the physical world, and indirect influence on Earth.

under.name: Breakthrough Law
under.description: States that levels alone cannot advance a being into a higher tier, which requires creating a skill belonging to that tier through experimentation, knowledge, creativity, execution, risk, and genuine new capability.

under.name: Mana and Technology
under.description: Describes how the Upgrade does not automatically disable modern technology, which remains functional and may evolve through System-recognized engineering and integration with magic.

under.name: Monster Dungeons
under.description: Covers Monster Dungeons, including their core definition, mixed manifestation, unknown origin, progressive activation, and fixed tier ceiling.

under.name: Core Definition
under.description: Defines a Monster Dungeon as a persistent origin region that introduces, produces, transforms, or sustains hostile life and elevated mana conditions, with varied possible appearances on upgraded Earth.

under.name: Mixed Manifestation
under.description: Some dungeons exist inside altered Earth locations while others are portals or breaches into spaces that do not obey ordinary geography, and no universal dungeon shape exists.

under.name: Unknown Origin
under.description: The true origin of dungeon creatures is unresolved, evidence is contradictory, and no theory is confirmed canon or explained by the System.

under.name: Progressive Activation
under.description: Earth's dungeon network does not activate at full global strength on Day Zero, with first Tier-0 dungeons manifesting immediately and additional dungeons and higher-tier regions emerging through later World Stages while advancement triggers remain unresolved.

under.name: Fixed Tier Ceiling
under.description: A dungeon cannot initially produce an entity or substance above its assigned tier, though the ceiling governs dungeon production rather than the permanent potential of what is produced.

under.name: Production Budget
under.description: Every active dungeon generates a renewable production budget that it may spend on different creature populations or store as dungeon pressure, with its nature influencing allocation.

under.name: Baseline Spawn Rates
under.description: Approximate maximum normal ceiling-tier output bands are given for dungeons spending most available budget at their own tier, with actual output modified by listed factors and described through output states.

under.name: Individual Creature Growth
under.description: Dungeon creatures follow the same universal growth laws as other System participants, with no hidden universal monster XP bonus and with explicit factors that may accelerate growth.

under.name: Independent Population Growth
under.description: Dungeon spawning and natural reproduction are separate sources of population, with reproduction bands and escaped populations developing through stages from Spawn Group to Polity.

under.name: Closure Law
under.description: No known world-bound being can permanently close a Monster Dungeon, although a dungeon may be suppressed, contained, delayed, monitored, exploited, temporarily sealed, or reduced in output.

under.name: Renewable Resources
under.description: Dungeons produce monsters and elevated concentrations of useful substances, with resource quality unable to exceed the dungeon's tier ceiling and output recovering over time.

under.name: Monster Tides
under.description: Describes Monster Tides as pressure overflow caused when dungeon output and surrounding hostile populations exceed local suppression capacity, with listed possible causes.

under.name: Monster Classification
under.description: Explains that "monster" is a contextual System classification associated with active hostility rather than a permanent species label.

under.name: The Five Great Peoples
under.description: Introduces the Five Great Peoples as broad origin categories—Baseline Humanity, Divergent Humanity, Awakened Earthborn, Dungeonborn, and Constructed/Anomalous Life—rather than unified political blocs.

under.name: 1. Baseline Humanity
under.description: Defines Baseline Humanity as humans who retain their original species identity despite System growth and remain culturally and politically divided.

under.name: 2. Divergent Humanity
under.description: Defines Divergent Humanity as humans transformed through class evolution, mana adaptation, mutation, undeath, technological integration, blessings, corruption, or deliberate biological change.

under.name: 3. Awakened Earthborn
under.description: Describes Awakened Earthborn as Earth-native nonhuman life recognized by the System as civilization-capable, with Tier 2 as the minimum threshold and no guarantee of sapience.

under.name: 4. Dungeonborn
under.description: Defines Dungeonborn as sapient beings first encountered within or through Monster Dungeons, with the label describing encounter location rather than true origin or moral nature.

under.name: 5. Constructed and Anomalous Life
under.description: Describes Constructed and Anomalous Life as beings fitting no stable biological lineage, such as awakened artificial intelligences, golems, artificial organisms, collective minds, living machines, system anomalies, or hybrid entities.

under.name: Political Order
under.description: Describes post-Upgrade political order as hybrid and dynamic, listing possible powers and stating that no fixed number of factions is predetermined and power emerges from actual control of resources and infrastructure.

under.name: System Currency
under.description: Covers the System's universal digital currency, including its nature, issuance methods, anti-farming rules, and purchasable System services.

under.name: Nature
under.description: The Nature section states that the System introduces a universal digital currency recorded through System status, cannot be conventionally counterfeited, and may be transferred through authorized System functions.

under.name: Currency Issuance
under.description: Currency Issuance lists ways new currency may enter circulation, including optional quests, achievements, discoveries, breakthroughs, dungeon suppression, rescues, defense, qualifying victories, and surrendered materials, with anti-farming rules.

under.name: System Services
under.description: System Services lists purchasable services such as marketplace listings, escrow, contracts, appraisal, licenses, transfers, storage, communication, registration, temporary No-Monster Zones, and Tier-6 contact, which remove currency from circulation.

under.name: System Knowledge and Skill Market
under.description: The System Knowledge and Skill Market section covers System-sold instruction, the complete catalog, purchasable instruction types, complexity, learning procedure, license types, and Base relationships.

under.name: Core Law
under.description: Core Law states that the System sells instruction rather than mastery and that purchased knowledge must be read, understood, practiced, tested, and integrated rather than placed directly into the buyer's mind.

under.name: Complete Catalog
under.description: Complete Catalog states that the full catalog of System-approved, non-Tier-6 learning material is visible from Day Zero and that visibility does not provide comprehension.

under.name: Types of Purchasable Instruction
under.description: Types of Purchasable Instruction lists catalog contents such as academic knowledge, combat methods, spell theory, skill manuals, recipes, formulas, blueprints, medical procedures, cultivation methods, monster studies, class theory, languages, research methods, and Base training.

under.name: Complexity and Power
under.description: Complexity and Power states that learning complexity rises with tier and potential impact and that higher-tier instruction generally has higher prices, more prerequisites, longer study, harder comprehension, greater practice demands, higher facility and material requirements, and more dangerous failure consequences.

under.name: Learning Procedure
under.description: Learning Procedure states that learning from purchased material follows normal time and noncombat rules and requires access, prerequisites, Phase Time, comprehension or training tasks, demonstration, and any required skill-creation or tier-breakthrough process.

under.name: License Types
under.description: License Types lists Personal, Party, Base, Guild, and Institutional access licenses, noting that broader licenses cost substantially more and that learned knowledge can be naturally remembered and taught.

under.name: Relationship to Bases
under.description: Relationship to Bases states that a Library, Archive, Training Hall, Laboratory, or similar Base room can host compatible licenses, improve their use, and require separate knowledge licenses.

under.name: Bases and Temporary Safe Zones
under.description: Bases and Temporary Safe Zones covers Base definition, conversion, inherent traits, rooms, construction, tiers, expansion, value, and temporary protection services.

under.name: Core Definition
under.description: Core Definition states that a Base is a high-cost System gift purchased with System currency and anchored to a building or controlled site to provide convenience, stability, and infrastructure.

under.name: Conversion
under.description: Conversion states that a person or recognized group must control a suitable building or site and pay the conversion price, after which the System repairs or stabilizes the structure, establishes the boundary and interface, records ownership, assigns tier and trait, and opens room slots.

under.name: Inherent Base Trait
under.description: Inherent Base Trait states that every Base receives a trait derived from the original purpose, structure, and history of the converted building, with examples such as Medical Infrastructure, Accelerated Study, and Fortification.

under.name: Room System
under.description: Room System states that rooms are specialized System modules purchased and constructed inside a Base and that they provide integrated facilities, tools, controlled environments, and applicable facility modifiers without creating materials, workers, mastery, or automatic products.

under.name: Construction and Expediting
under.description: Construction and Expediting states that purchased rooms and upgrades require construction time that increases with tier, size, complexity, expansion, and damage, and that additional currency may expedite construction without waiving prerequisites or physical inputs.

under.name: Room and Base Tiers
under.description: Room and Base Tiers states that every Base and specialized room has a tier, with rules on starting tier, room limits, Base advancement requirements, and improvements from advancing the Base.

under.name: Tiered Expansion
under.description: Tiered Expansion states that Base expansion changes with tier, from early use of the existing footprint to middle-tier rebuilding and outward expansion to high-tier spatial compression or extradimensional interiors.

under.name: Why Bases Are Valuable
under.description: Why Bases Are Valuable lists concentrated advantages such as specialized facilities, facility modifiers, storage, protected knowledge, marketplace access, administration, communication, crafting and research environments, rebuilding, temporary protection, Tier-6 communication anchoring, and settlement-scale support.

under.name: No-Monster Zones
under.description: A No-Monster Zone is a temporary hostility-suppression service centered on a recognized Base or other qualified location, not a permanent monster-destruction or dungeon-closing feature.

under.name: Tier-6 Contact
under.description: A qualified Base with the required room or System function may spend currency to open a mediated channel toward Tier-6 entities, but payment only opens the channel and does not compel or guarantee outcomes.

under.name: System Civilization Hierarchy
under.description: This section explains that Bases seed System-recognized civilizations and details civilization law, ranks, the Five-Branch pyramid, upgrade requirements, allegiance, benefits, and rank loss.

under.name: Civilization Law
under.description: Civilization Law states that Bases are the structural seeds from which System-recognized civilizations grow through nested subordinate Base networks available to all recognized peoples.

under.name: Civilization Ranks
under.description: Civilization Ranks lists Tier 0 through Tier 5 System civilization forms with required Core Base and minimum leader tiers, and notes Tier 6 has no world-bound form.

under.name: Five-Branch Pyramid
under.description: The Five-Branch Pyramid requires every civilization above Tier 0 to have five direct subordinate cores from the tier immediately below it, bringing their own lower-tier networks.

under.name: Upgrade Requirements
under.description: Upgrade Requirements lists the central Core Base, recognized leader, complete Five-Branch pyramid, infrastructure, stability, links, currency payment, and completed process needed for a civilization upgrade.

under.name: Counting and Allegiance
under.description: Counting and Allegiance explains that a subordinate Core can count toward only one superior hierarchy and that subservience may arise through voluntary treaty, accepted surrender, or completed conquest.

under.name: Voluntary Treaty
under.description: Voluntary Treaty describes a subordinate controller accepting an allegiance contract and joining the superior hierarchy under negotiated terms.

under.name: Accepted Surrender
under.description: Accepted Surrender describes the losing controller accepting transfer or vassal terms after conflict.

under.name: Completed Conquest
under.description: Completed Conquest describes how a conqueror may force integration by seizing the Base Core, defeating control, maintaining occupation, paying the System cost, and completing recognition, which grants control but not loyalty.

under.name: Network Benefits
under.description: Network Benefits describes coordination benefits unlocked by civilization rank, such as linked administration, communication, warnings, trade, knowledge licensing, safe zones, and disaster recovery.

under.name: Cohesion Crisis and Rank Loss
under.description: Cohesion Crisis and Rank Loss describes immediate degradation and a restoration period if a civilization falls below its rank requirements, followed by permanent downgrade if not restored.

under.name: Civilizational Function
under.description: Civilizational Function states that the hierarchy makes civilization structurally possible rather than peaceful, fair, or permanent, with Bases through Empires supporting survival under pressure.

under.name: Cosmology
under.description: Cosmology covers Tier-7, Tier-6 entities, followers and champions, and ascended beings in the Earth Upgrade world frame.

under.name: Tier-7 — Unknown Absolute
under.description: Tier-7 — Unknown Absolute describes the singular Tier-7 existence whose authority supersedes the Evolution System, with known facts and unknown motives or intentions.

under.name: Tier-6 Entities
under.description: Tier-6 Entities describes multiple external Tier-6 entities that cannot physically enter Earth, are unequal, have unknown hierarchies and agendas, and may influence events indirectly.

under.name: Followers and Champions
under.description: Followers and Champions describes how Tier-6 entities may maintain many followers and only one true champion at a time, with all granted power subject to System constraints.

under.name: Ascended Beings
under.description: Ascended Beings describes mortals completing Tier-6 Ascension joining the external layer and becoming subject to the prohibition against direct re-entry.

under.name: Dynamic Future
under.description: Dynamic Future lists possible but not guaranteed development paths such as government changes, guild states, corporations, religions, speciation, and civilizations, stating that laws are canon while the future is gameplay.

under.name: Intentionally Unresolved Questions
under.description: This section lists questions left open until established through play or later design, such as later World Stage triggers, dungeon details, Tier-6 and Tier-7 matters, surviving institutions, future powers, species recognition, currency, knowledge costs, and civilization-upgrade details, while noting unresolved does not mean secretly predetermined.

under.name: Event log
under.description: The Event log section states that no resolved world events are recorded.

under.name: Game log
under.description: The Game log section states that no player-facing game turns are recorded.
